classification.description: Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium)

origin_result.basis: No checks could be performed because the required bill of materials and declaration are missing.

procedure.step: Register the factory with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism; registration requires the factory to be outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added, and takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Prepare the required documents: proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, if a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
Log in to the ministry e-services portal and choose the Certificate of Origin for India service.
The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and conducting a factory visit.
Pay the certificate fee online; the fee depends on the invoice value and is in the range AED 10 to AED 200.
Receive approval, or a return with comments to correct, and print the approved certificate.
The competent authority issues the certificate before, at, or within five working days of export; it is valid for 12 months from issue and covers one import.
A certificate may be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from the date of shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 of India's certificate form.

Ensure the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. If a third party issues the invoice, indicate 'third-party invoicing'.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed.
The Indian importer keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing and must answer a customs request within 10 working days.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years starting from the end of the calendar year of issue.
An issued certificate can be amended once for a fee of AED 20; the invoice amount and destination cannot be changed.

caveats.note: The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty and, for lines in Table II, also the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti‑dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty only; no shipment value was provided, so only the rate difference is shown.
The '+' in the product-specific rule is interpreted as 'and', meaning both tests must pass; the agreement does not define '+'.
A factory in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is confirmed only in secondary sources.
There is a discrepancy between the agreement and India's certificate form regarding which box contains the remarks for retrospective issuance; India's form governs entry into India.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
